items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lennie Tristano was definitely one of them.

ctx.x: I just found another opening, another way to go, another feeling to have, another kind of sound to approach, another direction to move in. There were a lot of musicians that heard that and it had some kind of effect on them. Lennie Tristano was definitely one of them. In the ’40s, when everybody was playing the regular bebop, standards and stuff, he was extending on Pres’s music and really going out in another direction.
Is Jackie’s Bag the first recording where a lot of your new ideas about writing begin to show themselves?
